# Section 1: Overview
[INCLUDE: OVERVIEW OF MODELLING METHOD, DIFFICULTIES, LIMITATIONS, PERFORMANCE VS PM, ETC]

## Modelling objective:

We set ourselves the challenge of predicting the Premier League final rankings for the 2025/26 season. In our group, we will each build a model to achieve this. We will then compare each of our models performance vs our own custom performance metric. We hope to accurately predict the final rankings of each team. However, we decided that good models will prioritise accuracy in predicting which teams will finish in the top 5 postitons (and hence qualify for the champions league), and the bottom three positions (and hence get relegated) come the end of the season. This desire is represented by our custom performance metric discussed in the project doecument.

## Model discussion

I designed my model under the assumption that if you can predict the number of goals which will be scored in a game between any two teams, then you will be able to simualte the entire season of fixtures in order to build a predicted table. As becomes apparent through the building of my model, this may not be the optimal approach using my methods.

A common approach discussed in the existing literature (L. Gilch & S. Müller (2018), L.F. Maya et al. (2023), Maher (1982) etc...) is to model the goals scored by each of the competing teams as independent poisson random variables whose rate parameter is the expected number of goals. In their classic 1997 paper, Dixon & Coles introduced their adjustment to this model to change the probability distribution of low scoring results. 

I sought to use poisson regression with a log link function and a time-decay weighting in order to obtain the an attack and defence rating for each team in premier league. We obtained regression coefficients relating to these paramters, as well as a coefficient representing home advantage, and a baseline coefficient for our model.

I used the time weighting function $$w(x) = \begin{cases}
1 - \left(\dfrac{x}{c}\right)^p, & 0 \le d < c,\\
0, & d \ge c,
\end{cases}$$

where $x,c,\text{ and } p$ are parameters for representing the age of the observation, a specified cutoff, and a rate. We define $x$ relative to the most recent known date ie the date up to which we have perfect information. We use validation to obatin parameters $p$ and $c$ to be $\frac{1}{2}$ and $2555$.
Thus giving us the following weighting function:

```{r Plotting the weighting function, echo=FALSE, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
weight <- function(game_age, cut_off, power) {
  ifelse(game_age >= cut_off, 0, 1 - (game_age / cut_off)^power)}

library(ggplot2)
x_vals <- seq(0, 3000, by = 1)
power<- .5
cut_off <- 2555
df <- data.frame(x = x_vals, y = ifelse(x_vals >= cut_off, 0, 1 - (x_vals / 2555)^power) )

ggplot(df, aes(x=x, y=y))+
  geom_line()+
   labs(x = "Days ago", y = "Weighting", title = "Time decay of weighting") +
  theme_classic()
remove(df, power, x_vals)
```
This shows the model places more importance on the most recent data, before falling off with time since.

We then modelled the expected number of goals for home team i when facing team j as:

$X_{i,j} \sim \text{Poisson}(\lambda_{i,j})$, where $\lambda_{i,j} = \exp(\psi_H + \beta + \alpha_i  + \delta_j )$.

we modelled the number of goals for the away team j as:

$Y_{j,i} \sim \text{Poisson}(\mu_{j,i})$, where $\mu_{j,i} = \exp(\beta + \alpha_j  + \delta_i )$.

Here $\psi_H, \beta, \alpha_i, \delta_j$ represent home advantage effect, the baseline, attack rating of team i and defence rating of team j respectivley. 

We modelled the final scoreline as a joint distribution of these poisson random variables multiplied by the dixon coles adjustment:

$$f_{X,Y}(x,y) =
\frac{e^{-(\lambda_{i,j}+\mu_{j,i})}
\lambda_{i,j}^{x}\mu_{j,i}^{y}}{x!y!}
\times
\tau(x,y,\lambda_{i,j},\mu_{j,i},\rho),$$

where the correction term $\tau$ is given by:

$$\tau(x,y,\lambda,\mu,\rho)=
\begin{cases}
1-\lambda\mu\rho & \text{if } (x,y)=(0,0),\\
1+\lambda\rho & \text{if } (x,y)=(0,1),\\
1+\mu\rho & \text{if } (x,y)=(1,0),\\
1-\rho & \text{if } (x,y)=(1,1),\\
1 & \text{otherwise}.
\end{cases}$$

This raises what I expect to be the first major limitation of my modelling procedure. I used regression to estimate the team ratings according to the poisson model for goals. I then modelled games under the dixon-coles model. Now although closely related, they are not the same. If time allowed, I would look to obtain my rating coefficients via the maximisation of a custom likelihood function for the dixon-coles model.

The next difficulty I had was obtaining ratings for newly promoted teams into the premier league. As such, I took the lead from dixon-coles (1997) again, and ran the same regression on the corresponding championship seasons. Thus, we obtain ratings from the championship for teams prior to their promotion to the premier league. Now you can see the same problem arising for teams newly promoted to the championship from league 1, and then in league 1 for teams promoted from league 2 etc... I mitigated this by setting as a standard that teams promoted to championship from league 1 would have median championship ratings.

A further difficulty I had was making ratings obtained in the championship, by teams whom were then promoted, play with the ratings of teams already in the premier league. Intuitivley you would expect the ratings to not be directly transferable since its a big fish small pond to small fish big pond situation. I attempted to retain information already gathered about promoted teams by scaling their ratings by found parameters upon start of a new season. 

This scaling approach meant that I had to centre the ratings for teams around their arithmetic mean. Thus our benchmark teams in each league recieved ratings of 1 for attack and defence.

I used the same scaling trick with different parameters to deal with teams relegated from the premier league to the championship.

## Other limitations

Like in the markets, in football prediction, I have found that past performance is always indicative of future results, apart from when it isn't... which turns out to be often. A major limitation of my model is that it is truly dependent on past scorelines as indicator of quality. Now this is fair to some degree, but it is clearly not capturing the full picture. In a future attempt I would look to include more features in my train data. I considered playing with pm player ratings as discussed in J. Lopez Pena et al.'s 2017 paper: Plus-Minus Player Ratings for Soccer. I believed that this would allow me to form an accurate metric for measuring team strengths, while accounting for squad changes through injuries and transfers, two factors which can have dramatic impacts on team performance over short time period. I did not pursue this option to any grate depth due to it's potential to fail dramatically.

## Expanding rolling windows for validation
Given our "x_all" data, we now create expanding rolling window dataframes in order to obtain our coefficients and to tune our hyper parameters. We first find dates which we can safely start and end seasons on while keeping each season disjoint. Note that this is quite important for model fitting.

We choose a season end date of July 27th and a season start date of the 28th of july. That is, each season runs from 28/07/20(yy) to 27/07/20(yy+1). For each test window, we will create two validation sets: one in which we predict the entire validation period, ie complete season prediction, and another where we predict all games after a cut-off period.

```{r generate rolling window validation, warning=FALSE, include=FALSE}
generate_validation <- function(ech_all, epl_all, year, cutoff) {
  start_date <- as.Date(paste0(year, "-07-28"))
  end_date   <- as.Date(paste0(year + 1, "-07-27"))

  # all data before the season begins
  historical_ech <- ech_all %>%
    filter(Date < start_date)
  historical_epl <- epl_all %>%
    filter(Date < start_date)

  # fixtures/results belonging to the target season
  target_ech <- ech_all %>%
    filter(Date >= start_date, Date <= end_date)
  target_epl <- epl_all %>%
    filter(Date >= start_date, Date <= end_date)

  # complete season 
  complete_season <- list(
    ech_train = historical_ech, epl_train = historical_epl,
    ech_test  = target_ech, epl_test  = target_epl)

  # in season
  cutoff <- as.Date(cutoff)

  in_season <- list(
    ech_train = ech_all %>%
      filter(Date < cutoff),
    epl_train = epl_all %>%
      filter(Date < cutoff),
    ech_test = target_ech %>%
      filter(Date >= cutoff),
    epl_test = target_epl %>%
      filter(Date >= cutoff))
   

  return(list(
    complete_season = complete_season,
    in_season = in_season))
}

generate_rolling_validation <- function(epl_all, ech_all, years, cutoff_month, cutoff_day) {

  rolling_window_sets <- lapply(years, function(year){
    cutoff <- as.Date(sprintf(  "%d-%02d-%02d",
      year, cutoff_month, cutoff_day))
      
    generate_validation(ech_all, epl_all, year, cutoff)}) 
  
  names(rolling_window_sets) <- years
  return(rolling_window_sets)}
```

We construct the following rolling window data sets:

```{r}
# Important: this gives 2015/16 to 2024/25. We can then test on 2025/26.
```

We have our basic rolling window data_sets, however, we now need to convert them into a usable form in order to use them for validation. We introduce the following code to do this:   

```{r rolling window conversion}
# This function splits the home and away training data
def_home_away_split_train <- function(data) {
home_data <- data %>%
  transmute(Date, Team = HomeTeam, Opponent = AwayTeam, Goals = FTHG, Home = 1, obvs_weight = obvs_weight)

away_data <- data %>%
  transmute(Date, Team = AwayTeam, Opponent = HomeTeam, Goals = FTAG, Home = 0, obvs_weight = obvs_weight)

train_goal_data <- bind_rows(home_data, away_data)

return(train_goal_data)}

# This function splits the home and away validation data
# note that it does not retain the obvs weight data, this is 
# needed due quirks with d_c game model  
def_home_away_split_validation <- function(data) {
home_data <- data %>%
  transmute(Date, Team = HomeTeam, Opponent = AwayTeam, Goals = FTHG, Home = 1)

away_data <- data %>%
  transmute(Date, Team = AwayTeam, Opponent = HomeTeam, Goals = FTAG, Home = 0)

validation_goal_data <- bind_rows(home_data, away_data)

return(validation_goal_data)}


# This helper function pulls the teams in a comp given, we use
# it to help 
get_season_teams <- function(data, year) {

  start_date <- as.Date(paste0(year, "-07-28"))
  end_date   <- as.Date(paste0(year + 1, "-07-27"))

  season_data <- data %>%
    filter(Date >= start_date, Date <= end_date)

  unique(c(
    as.character(season_data$HomeTeam),
    as.character(season_data$AwayTeam)))}

# we build this function to adjust the division ratings when
# teams move between leagues
adjust_division_ratings <- function(
    epl_ratings, ech_ratings, epl_all,
    ech_all, year, a_p, d_p, a_c, d_c,
    current_epl = NULL, current_ech = NULL) {

  # Use supplied current season teams where available.
  # Otherwise, obtain them from the historical data.
  if (is.null(current_epl)) {
    current_epl <- get_season_teams(epl_all, year)}

  if (is.null(current_ech)) {
    current_ech <- get_season_teams(ech_all, year)}

  previous_epl <- get_season_teams(epl_all, year - 1)
  previous_ech <- get_season_teams(ech_all, year - 1)


  # promoted and relegated sides
  promoted_to_epl <- intersect(current_epl, previous_ech)
  relegated_to_ech <- intersect(current_ech, previous_epl)

  # league 1 to champ
  new_ech_entrants <- setdiff(
    current_ech, union(previous_ech, previous_epl))

  # retreive ratings func to obtain the teams ratings
  get_rows <- function(teams, ratings) {
    idx <- match(teams, ratings$team_names)
    ratings[idx, , drop = FALSE]}

  # prem teams
  epl_stayers <- setdiff(current_epl, promoted_to_epl)

  epl_adjusted <- get_rows(epl_stayers, epl_ratings)

  # champ to prem teams
  promoted_ratings <- get_rows(promoted_to_epl, ech_ratings)

  promoted_ratings$att_rating <-
    promoted_ratings$att_rating * a_p

  promoted_ratings$def_rating <-
    promoted_ratings$def_rating * d_p

  epl_adjusted <- bind_rows(
    epl_adjusted, promoted_ratings)

  # champ teams
  ech_stayers <- setdiff(
    current_ech,
    c(relegated_to_ech, new_ech_entrants))

  ech_adjusted <- get_rows(ech_stayers, ech_ratings)

  # relegated to champ transfer
  relegated_ratings <- get_rows(relegated_to_ech, epl_ratings)

  relegated_ratings$att_rating <-
    relegated_ratings$att_rating * a_c

  relegated_ratings$def_rating <-
    relegated_ratings$def_rating * d_c

  ech_adjusted <- bind_rows(
    ech_adjusted, relegated_ratings)

  # new champ teams
  if (length(new_ech_entrants) > 0) {

    median_attack <- median(ech_ratings$att_rating)
    median_defence <- median(ech_ratings$def_rating)

    new_ratings <- data.frame(
      team_names = new_ech_entrants,
      att_rating = median_attack, def_rating = median_defence)

    ech_adjusted <- bind_rows(
      ech_adjusted, new_ratings)}

  # this makes sure ratings follow the current season's
  # team order.
  epl_adjusted <- epl_adjusted[
    match(current_epl, epl_adjusted$team_names),]

  ech_adjusted <- ech_adjusted[
    match(current_ech, ech_adjusted$team_names),]

  return(list(epl_ratings = epl_adjusted,
    ech_ratings = ech_adjusted,
    promoted_to_epl = promoted_to_epl,
    relegated_to_ech = relegated_to_ech,
    new_ech_entrants = new_ech_entrants))}

# We add this function to extract ratings
extract_ratings <- function(model) {

  teams <- model$xlevels$Team
  coefs <- coef(model)
  
  # initialise each teams log_attack rating
  attack_log <- setNames(rep(0, length(teams)), teams)
  defence_log <- setNames(rep(0, length(teams)), teams)
  
  # now we extract ratings
  for (team in teams) {

    attack_name <- paste0("Team", team)
    defence_name <- paste0("Opponent", team)

    if (attack_name %in% names(coefs)) {     # since baseline team 
      # has no coefs,
      attack_log[team] <- coefs[attack_name]} # we only update 
      # teams with coefs

    if (defence_name %in% names(coefs)) {
      defence_log[team] <- coefs[defence_name]}}
  
  # center the log ratings so that prem and champ ratings can be
  # scaled later
  mean_attack <- mean(attack_log)
  mean_defence <- mean(defence_log)

  ratings <- data.frame(team_names = teams,
    att_rating = exp(attack_log - mean_attack),
    def_rating = exp(defence_log - mean_defence))
  
  baseline <- unname(coefs["(Intercept)"]) + mean_attack +
    mean_defence
  home_advantage <- unname(coefs["Home"])
  
  return(list(ratings = ratings, baseline = baseline, 
              home_advantage = home_advantage))}


# Okie dokie, finally we prepare our windows, and fit our 
# poisson regression in order to obtain ratings.

# This func build the split training data.
prepare_training_goals <- function(data, known_date, cut_off, power) {train_data <- data %>%
    filter(Date < known_date) %>%
    mutate(days_ago = as.numeric(known_date - Date)) %>%
    filter(days_ago < cut_off) %>%
    mutate(obvs_weight = weight(days_ago, cut_off, power))
  def_home_away_split_train(train_data)}

# this function then fits our regression to the training data
fit_division_models <- function(epl_train, ech_train,
    known_date, cut_off, power) {
  
  # we prepare the data
  train_epl_goals <- prepare_training_goals(
    epl_train, known_date, cut_off, power)

  train_ech_goals <- prepare_training_goals(
    ech_train, known_date, cut_off, power)

  # fit our separate Poisson GLMs onto the training data
  epl_goal_model <- glm(
    Goals ~ Home + Team + Opponent,
    family = poisson(link = "log"),
    data = train_epl_goals,
    weights = obvs_weight)

  ech_goal_model <- glm(
    Goals ~ Home + Team + Opponent,
    family = poisson(link = "log"),
    data = train_ech_goals,
    weights = obvs_weight)

  # then extract our team ratings
  epl_model <- extract_ratings(epl_goal_model)
  ech_model <- extract_ratings(ech_goal_model)

  return(list(
    epl_ratings = epl_model$ratings,
    ech_ratings = ech_model$ratings,

    epl_baseline = epl_model$baseline,
    epl_home_advantage = epl_model$home_advantage,

    ech_baseline = ech_model$baseline,
    ech_home_advantage = ech_model$home_advantage,
    
     epl_goal_model = epl_goal_model,
     ech_goal_model = ech_goal_model))}
```

We now have our models fitted to the training data. We want to be able to evaluate our models under our Dixon-Coles game model. We want to use our fitted models ratings to then predict test fixtures under the D-C scoreline adjustment. The end goal being to vary different parameter choices and compare the accuracy of our prediction on the validation data. Note that our objective is to minimise the MAE.

```{r Model evaluation under Dixon-Coles gamemodel}
# First we get the code which will give the probability of
# seeing a scoreline under the dc game model
dixon_coles_probs <- function(team_ratings, home_team, away_team, baseline, home_advantage, rho = -0.05, max_goals = 7) {

  # get team ratings
  home_att <- team_ratings$att_rating[team_ratings$team_names == home_team]
  home_def <- team_ratings$def_rating[team_ratings$team_names == home_team]
  away_att <- team_ratings$att_rating[team_ratings$team_names == away_team]
  away_def <- team_ratings$def_rating[team_ratings$team_names == away_team]
  
  
  # calculate poisson rates from ratings
  
  lambda <- exp(baseline + home_advantage) * home_att * away_def #home rate
  mu <- exp(baseline) * away_att * home_def # away rate
  
  goals <- 0:max_goals #we truncate the number of goals we may 
  # observe when setting a scoreline. Note that although
  # precedented, teams scoring more than max goals is very rare.
  # further we assume that if it were the case that a team scored
  # so many goals, then our model should already favour them
  # greatly since they presumably have far higher ratings than
  # their opponents.  

  # get the scoreline prob under independent poisson goals
  # assumption 
  probs <- outer(dpois(goals, lambda), dpois(goals, mu))

  # correction
  probs[1, 1] <- probs[1, 1] * (1 - lambda * mu * rho)
  probs[1, 2] <- probs[1, 2] * (1 + lambda * rho)
  probs[2, 1] <- probs[2, 1] * (1 + mu * rho)
  probs[2, 2] <- probs[2, 2] * (1 - rho)

  # since we truncate the scoreline grid, we normalise our 
  # 'probs' so that they sum to 1. 
  probs <- probs / sum(probs)
  
  return(probs)}

# now we introduce the code to evaluate a single fixture under our dc game model:
predict_dc_fixture <- function(home_team, away_team,
                               team_ratings, baseline,
                               home_advantage,
                               rho = -0.05, max_goals = 7) {

  # extracts the probs of results given team ratings
  probs <- dixon_coles_probs(team_ratings = team_ratings,
                             home_team = home_team,
                             away_team = away_team,
                             baseline = baseline,
                             home_advantage = home_advantage,
                             rho = rho, max_goals = max_goals)

  # expected goals under model used in model validation
  goals <- 0:(nrow(probs) - 1)

  expected_home_goals <- sum(rowSums(probs) * goals)
  expected_away_goals <- sum(colSums(probs) * goals)

  # the prob of a match outcome (used later for league table)
  prob_home_win <- sum(probs[row(probs) > col(probs)])
  prob_draw <- sum(probs[row(probs) == col(probs)])
  prob_away_win <- sum(probs[row(probs) < col(probs)])

  data.frame( expected_home_goals = expected_home_goals,
    expected_away_goals = expected_away_goals, 
    prob_home_win =prob_home_win,
    prob_draw = prob_draw, prob_away_win = prob_away_win)}


# We create a callable function which will predict fixtures
# under the d_c model, given team ratings.
evaluate_dc_fixtures <- function(data, team_ratings,
    baseline, home_advantage, rho = -0.05, max_goals = 10){
  
  # applies to each fixture the predict_dc code 
  predictions <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(data)), function(i) {

    predict_dc_fixture(home_team = data$HomeTeam[i],
      away_team = data$AwayTeam[i],
      team_ratings = team_ratings,
      baseline = baseline,
      home_advantage = home_advantage,
      rho = rho,
      max_goals = max_goals)})

  predictions <- bind_rows(predictions)
  
  # We then take out only the columns which we care about
  results <- bind_cols(data %>% 
                         select(Date, HomeTeam, AwayTeam, 
                                FTHG, FTAG), predictions)

  # Combine home and away observations
  actual <- c(results$FTHG, results$FTAG)

  predicted <- c(results$expected_home_goals,
    results$expected_away_goals)

  errors <- actual - predicted

  metrics <- data.frame(n_fixtures = nrow(data),
    n_observations = length(actual),
    mean_actual =  mean(actual), mean_predicted 
    =mean(predicted),
    MAE = mean(abs(errors)), RMSE = sqrt(mean(errors^2)))

  return(list(metrics = metrics, predictions = results))}

```

Okay, we are almost at the point where we can begin to tune our parameter choices over the validation data. We will look to minimise MAE as our optimisation objective. Reiterating again that we are going to assume that an increase in the accuracy of our goal predictions will cause an increase in the accuracy of our league table by the end of the season.

We will first tune the league adjustment scalars. We will run procedure over complete season data, then again for in season data. We will aggregate the MSE and RMSE and choose the the set of scalars which result in the minimal realised values of these. 

```{r tuning the league transition scalars}
# We choose our validation mode since we can either validate on 
# a whole unseen season, or just complete a seen season.

validation_mode <- "complete_season"

# choose the years from which we want to produce fitted models
years <- 2015:2023

# time weight params (to be tuned seperatley later)
power <- 3
cut_off <- 730

# dc params (rho also to be tuned)
rho <- -0.05
max_goals <- 7

# we will also get the known date (note this needs to be changed if we change the season start or the in_season_cut date)

# function to get the known date variable 
get_known_date <- function(year, mode) {
  
  if (mode == "complete_season") {
    return(as.Date(sprintf("%d-07-27", year)))}
  if (mode == "in_season") {
    return(as.Date(sprintf("%d-11-01", year)))}}

# also we will prefit the glm model to the data
prepare_rolling_models <- function(rw_validation_sets, years,
                                   mode, cut_off, power) {

  results <- lapply(years, function(year) {
    validation <-rw_validation_sets[[as.character(year)]][[mode]]

    # Use the start of the target season as the information date
    known_date <- as.Date(paste0(year, "-07-28"))

    fitted_models <- fit_division_models(
      epl_train = validation$epl_train,
      ech_train = validation$ech_train,
      known_date = known_date,
      cut_off = cut_off, power = power)

    list(year = year, known_date = known_date,
      fitted_models = fitted_models,epl_test = validation$epl_test,
      ech_test = validation$ech_test)})

  names(results) <- as.character(years)

  return(results)}

# we now create our rolling modesl. We pre-fit these since when we
# are testing our scaling params, we needn't re fit the model every
# time.

rolling_models <- prepare_rolling_models(
  rw_validation_sets = rw_validation_sets, years = years,
  mode = validation_mode, cut_off = cut_off, power = power)

# We now make code which can obtain the MSE for each term
score_dc_fixtures <- function(
    data, team_ratings, baseline, home_advantage,
    rho = -0.05,max_goals = 7) {

  # obtain predictions
  predictions <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(data)), function(i) {
    
  # use the predict dc function to get predictions for each fixture
  predict_dc_fixture( home_team = data$HomeTeam[i],
    away_team = data$AwayTeam[i], team_ratings = team_ratings,
    baseline = baseline, home_advantage = home_advantage,
    rho = rho, max_goals = max_goals)})
  
  # Collate the predictions
  predictions <- bind_rows(predictions)

  # Collect actual results
  actual <- c(data$FTHG, data$FTAG)

  predicted <- c( predictions$expected_home_goals,
                  predictions$expected_away_goals)

  # Calc errors
  errors <- actual - predicted
  
  return(list(n = length(errors), 
    absolute_error_sum = sum(abs(errors)),
    squared_error_sum = sum(errors^2),
    MAE = mean(abs(errors)),
    RMSE = sqrt(mean(errors^2))))}
```

Okie dokie; we are finally in the position where we can find our errors in predictions under different parameters. We will do so below to compare different input parameters.

```{r evaluation of transition params}
evaluate_transition_parameters <- function(
    a_p, d_p, a_c, d_c,
    rolling_models,
    epl_all,
    ech_all,
    rho = -0.05,
    max_goals = 5) {

  yearly_results <- lapply(rolling_models, function(validation) {

    year <- validation$year
    fitted <- validation$fitted_models

    # apply the adjustments
    adjusted <- adjust_division_ratings(
      epl_ratings = fitted$epl_ratings,
      ech_ratings = fitted$ech_ratings,
      epl_all = epl_all, ech_all = ech_all,
      year = year, a_p = a_p, d_p = d_p,
      a_c = a_c, d_c = d_c)

    # eval prem results
    epl_score <- score_dc_fixtures(
      data = validation$epl_test,
      team_ratings = adjusted$epl_ratings,
      baseline = fitted$epl_baseline,
      home_advantage = fitted$epl_home_advantage,
      rho = rho, max_goals = max_goals)

    # evaluate champ predictions
    ech_score <- score_dc_fixtures(
      data = validation$ech_test,
      team_ratings = adjusted$ech_ratings,
      baseline = fitted$ech_baseline,
      home_advantage = fitted$ech_home_advantage, rho = rho,
      max_goals = max_goals)

    # combine the scores over seasons
    total_n <- epl_score$n + ech_score$n

    total_abs <- epl_score$absolute_error_sum +
      ech_score$absolute_error_sum

    total_sq <- epl_score$squared_error_sum +
      ech_score$squared_error_sum

    data.frame( year = year, EPL_MAE = epl_score$MAE,
      EPL_RMSE = epl_score$RMSE, ECH_MAE = ech_score$MAE,
      ECH_RMSE = ech_score$RMSE,
      Combined_MAE = total_abs / total_n,
      Combined_RMSE = sqrt(total_sq / total_n),
      n_observations = total_n, absolute_error_sum = total_abs,
      squared_error_sum = total_sq)})

  yearly_results <- bind_rows(yearly_results)

  # overall results
  total_n <- sum(yearly_results$n_observations)
  total_abs <- sum(yearly_results$absolute_error_sum)
  total_sq <- sum(yearly_results$squared_error_sum)

  summary <- data.frame(
    a_p = a_p, d_p = d_p, a_c = a_c, d_c = d_c,
    Mean_EPL_MAE = mean(yearly_results$EPL_MAE),
    Mean_ECH_MAE = mean(yearly_results$ECH_MAE),
    Mean_Combined_MAE = mean(yearly_results$Combined_MAE),
    Pooled_Combined_MAE = total_abs / total_n,
    Pooled_Combined_RMSE = sqrt(total_sq / total_n),
    SD_Combined_MAE = sd(yearly_results$Combined_MAE))

  return(list(summary = summary, yearly_results = yearly_results))}
```

We now define our parameter grid. Note this grid is very coarse. we may be able to refine this later given a ball park. We start with such a small grid since our current process is computationally murderous in the current setup (apologies), im going to impose that champ team ratings can only get worse going to prem. I will make no restriction on prem to champ since back to back relegations are not unheard of however back to back top finishes over leagues is uncommon to the point of non-existent.

We will not run the following code since it takes ages to knit. We will however source the results table for your viewing pleasure.

# Tuning power and cut_off

For ease we will use a rho value of -0.13 as found in the blog https://opisthokonta.net/?p=890. We may look to find our own parameter value if the time constraints allow, but for now this will suffice. We do, however, need to tune the power and cut_off parameters for our time weighting functions. We will use a coarse grid initially for this which we may refine if time allows.

Again, this takes a rather long time to run. Hence, we will just call the results.
```{r weight tuner, eval=FALSE, include=FALSE}
power_grid <- c(0.5, 1, 1.5, 2, 2.5, 3, 4)

cut_off_grid <- c(365, 730, 1095, 1460,1825, 2190, 2555)

weighting_grid <- expand.grid(power = power_grid, cut_off = cut_off_grid)

weighting_results <- vector("list", nrow(weighting_grid))

for (i in seq_len(nrow(weighting_grid))) {
  current_power <- weighting_grid$power[i]
  current_cut_off <- weighting_grid$cut_off[i]

  cat("\nCombination", i, "of", nrow(weighting_grid), 
      "| Power:", current_power,

    rw_validation_sets = rw_validation_sets,
```

# Section 4: Testing our model
We now look to predict the 2025-26 season table with our trained model. We load our test data.


```{r Predicting the league, include=FALSE}
predict_fixtures <- function(
    fixtures,
    team_ratings,
    baseline,
    home_advantage,
    rho = -0.13,
    max_goals = 7) {

  results <- lapply(seq_len(nrow(fixtures)), function(i) {

    home <- fixtures$HomeTeam[i]
    away <- fixtures$AwayTeam[i]
# call dc func to give scoreline probs
    probs <- dixon_coles_probs(
      team_ratings = team_ratings,
      home_team = home,
      away_team = away,
      baseline = baseline,
      home_advantage = home_advantage,
      rho = rho,
      max_goals = max_goals)

    goals <- 0:max_goals
# calc expected home goals
    expected_home <- sum(probs * matrix(
      goals,
      nrow = length(goals),
      ncol = length(goals)))
# calc expected away goals
    expected_away <- sum(probs * matrix(
      goals,
      nrow = length(goals),
      ncol = length(goals),
      byrow = TRUE))
# give probs of the three match outcomes
    home_win <- sum(probs[row(probs) > col(probs)])
    draw <- sum(diag(probs))
    away_win <- sum(probs[row(probs) < col(probs)])
# gives most likely outcome
    most_likely <- which(
      probs == max(probs), arr.ind = TRUE)[1, ]
# colate all of the predictions
    data.frame(Date = fixtures$Date[i],
      HomeTeam = home, AwayTeam = away,
      Expected_Home_Goals = expected_home,
      Expected_Away_Goals = expected_away,
      Predicted_Score = paste0(
        most_likely[1] - 1, "-",
        most_likely[2] - 1),
      Home_Win_Prob = home_win, Draw_Prob = draw,
      Away_Win_Prob = away_win,
      Expected_Home_Points = 3 * home_win + draw,
      Expected_Away_Points = 3 * away_win + draw)})

  bind_rows(results)}
# get predictions for epl
epl_predictions <- predict_fixtures(
  epl_test,
  final_ratings$epl_ratings,
  final_models$epl_baseline,
  final_models$epl_home_advantage)

ech_predictions <- predict_fixtures(
  ech_test,
  final_ratings$ech_ratings,
  final_models$ech_baseline,
  final_models$ech_home_advantage)

compare_league_tables <- function(fixtures, predictions) {

  # predicted home team conts
  predicted_home <- data.frame(
    Team = predictions$HomeTeam, P = 1,
    Expected_Pts = predictions$Expected_Home_Points,
    Expected_GF = predictions$Expected_Home_Goals,
    Expected_GA = predictions$Expected_Away_Goals)

  # predicted away team conts
  predicted_away <- data.frame(
    Team = predictions$AwayTeam, P = 1,
    Expected_Pts = predictions$Expected_Away_Points,
    Expected_GF = predictions$Expected_Away_Goals,
    Expected_GA = predictions$Expected_Home_Goals)
# form predicted table
  predicted_table <- bind_rows(
    predicted_home, predicted_away) %>%
    group_by(Team) %>%
    summarise(
      P = sum(P), Expected_Pts = sum(Expected_Pts),
      Expected_GF = sum(Expected_GF), Expected_GA =
        sum(Expected_GA),Expected_GD = Expected_GF - Expected_GA,
      .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(Expected_Pts), 
            desc(Expected_GD), desc(Expected_GF)) %>%
    mutate(Predicted_Rank = row_number())

  # get actual
  completed <- fixtures 

  actual_home <- data.frame( Team = completed$HomeTeam,
    GF = completed$FTHG, GA = completed$FTAG)

  actual_away <- data.frame(Team = completed$AwayTeam,
    GF = completed$FTAG, GA = completed$FTHG)
# get act rsults
  actual_results <- bind_rows(actual_home, actual_away) %>%
    mutate(W = as.integer(GF > GA),
      D = as.integer(GF == GA),
      L = as.integer(GF < GA),
      Pts = 3 * W + D)
# form actual table
  actual_table <- actual_results %>%
    group_by(Team) %>%
    summarise(P = n(), W = sum(W), D = sum(D),
      L = sum(L), GF = sum(GF), GA = sum(GA),
      GD = GF - GA, Pts = sum(Pts), .groups = "drop") %>%
    arrange(desc(Pts), desc(GD), desc(GF)) %>%
    mutate(Actual_Rank = dplyr::row_number())

  # merge the two table 
  comparison <- full_join(predicted_table, actual_table,
    by = "Team", suffix = c("_Predicted", "_Actual")) %>%
    mutate(Rank_Difference = Predicted_Rank - Actual_Rank) %>%
    arrange(Actual_Rank)

  return(list(comparison = comparison))}
```

```{r creating league table}
epl_tables <- compare_league_tables(
  fixtures = epl_test,
  predictions = epl_predictions)
# we'll have a look of course we'll have a look.
print(epl_tables$comparison)
```
We can also run our predicted table and the actual table through our performance metric to get our model score:

```{r performance metric}
pm <- function(predicted, actual) {
  
  n <- length(actual)
  # Identify the top five teams
  P5 <- which(predicted <= 5)
  A5 <- which(actual <= 5)

  # Calculate overlap between predicted and actual top five
  overlap <- length(intersect(P5, A5)) / 5

  # Identify bottom three positions
  bottom3 <- (n - 2):n

  wt <- numeric(n)

  for (i in 1:n) {

    p <- predicted[i]
    a <- actual[i]

    d <- abs(p - a)

    if (a <= 5) { # Actual position is in the top five
      
      if (p == a) {
        w <- 1

      } else if (p <= 5) {
        w <- overlap

      } else {
        w <- -(1 - exp(-d))
      }

    } else {# Actual position is outside the top five

      if (a %in% bottom3) {# Actual team is in the bottom three

        if (p %in% bottom3) {
          w <- 1

        } else {
          w <- -(1 - exp(-d))
        }

      } else if (p <= 5) {# Incorrectly predicted in the top five
        
        w <- -(1 - exp(-d))

      } else if (p == a) {# Correctly predicted outside the top five

        w <- 0.5

      } else {# Incorrectly predicted outside the top five
        k <- 0.1
        w <- -(1 - exp(-k * d))
      }
    }

    wt[i] <- w
  }

  return(sum(wt))
}

```

We then feed this into our adjusted function to give our final score:

```{r}
pm_adjusted <- function(predicted, actual, number_features, lambda=0.01) {
  
  upper <- pm(predicted = epl_tables$comparison$Actual_Rank, actual= epl_tables$comparison$Actual_Rank)

lower <- pm(predicted = 21- epl_tables$comparison$Actual_Rank,  actual= epl_tables$comparison$Actual_Rank)

  prediction_score <- (pm(predicted, actual) -lower)/ (upper - lower)
  
  feature_penalisation <- exp(-lambda * number_features)
  
  model_score <- prediction_score * feature_penalisation
  
  return(model_score)
}
```

Our overall score for predicting the season is given by 0.26154.

```{r model score}
pm_adjusted(predicted= epl_tables$comparison$Predicted_Rank,
            actual= epl_tables$comparison$Actual_Rank, 
            number_features= 4, lambda = 0.01 )

```
